title: Your own pitch names the thread after the investor, never after you

objects.subject: Kitebird - seed round
objects.body:
Hi Ira,

Kitebird is raising a seed round to bring AI scheduling to small clinics - 14 are live. Would you take a look at our deck this week?

Meera

questions.text: Take a look at the deck this week
questions.quote: Would you take a look at our deck this week?

business_facts.subject: thread
business_facts.quote: Kitebird is raising a seed round

notes: STEP-04. Production: the founder's own pitch threads were named '<the founder> - <the pitch>' (the business claim's sender, whatever the direction) and never renamed. The acceptance checks the thread's name.

facts.claim: On the eleventh of August the founder wrote to Ira at Northwind that Kitebird is raising a seed round to bring AI scheduling to small clinics, with clinics already live, and asked Ira to look at the deck this week.
The file lists that ask as open, with us waiting on Northwind, and names the move as theirs.
The pitch is the only touch in the file; no answer from Ira is in it yet.
The brief names no kind of work for Northwind; the engine filed it as an investor relationship under fundraising.

inferences.claim: Northwind is an investor being pitched for the seed round.
The move is Ira's: the founder has asked, and the week she named for a look is still running.

hypotheses.proposition: The deck went with the mail.
hypotheses.needs: The founder's word, or the sent mail's attachment — the file shows only its words.

unknowns.question: Whether the deck was attached or linked in the pitch.
unknowns.relevance: If not, Ira has nothing to look at, and the ask cannot be met as written.

unknowns.question: Who Ira is at Northwind, and whether the pitch was cold or introduced.
unknowns.relevance: A cold pitch's silence is the default; an introduced one's silence is a question for the person who introduced it.

unknowns.question: Whether Northwind invests at seed in clinic software.
unknowns.relevance: A poor fit makes waiting pointless; a good one makes a later note worth a new fact.

frames.primary: A seed pitch just sent: you asked Northwind to look at the deck this week, and the move is theirs.
rivals: A cold pitch that never becomes a meeting.
An introduced pitch, where a slow answer is a question for the connector rather than for Ira.

proposed_kind.why: The founder's mail pitches Kitebird's seed round to Ira at Northwind and asks for a look at the deck, and the engine already treats the file as an investor relationship.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, the founder's own ask sets the clock: a look at the deck this week.
expected_vs_actual.actual: The pitch went out on the eleventh of August; nothing has come back yet, and the week the founder named is still running.

scenarios.do_nothing: Ira reads the pitch in their own time; if Northwind is interested, an answer comes within the week you named.
scenarios.act: Chasing before the week is out would press an investor who has not yet had a fair chance to look.
scenarios.best: Ira looks at the deck and asks for a call.
scenarios.worst: The pitch goes unread and the week passes in silence.
signals_to_watch: An answer or a meeting request from Ira.
The week the founder named passing with no word from Northwind.

reasons: Raising the seed round is the brief's first goal, and Northwind is a fund being pitched for it.
The pitch went out the same day, and the move is Northwind's.
One later note remains available if the week passes.

answer.alternative: If the founder finds the deck was not attached, send it at once with one line — that is a fix, not a chase.
answer.wait_or_stop: Wait out the week the founder named. If nothing comes, send one short note that carries something new; if that draws nothing, stop and treat Northwind as a no for this round.
answer.done_when: Ira answers — a call booked, a question, or a pass.
